notes: Take before starting Project 2 (FastAPI + React). Covers what each HTTP method means, status codes, and RESTful URL design.

questions.question: You want to retrieve the film with id 42 without changing anything on the server. Which HTTP method should you use?
questions.explanation: `GET` is for reading. It is *safe*: a GET request should never change data on the server.

questions.question: Which request is the conventional RESTful way to **create** a new film?
options: `POST /films` with the new film's data in the request body
questions.explanation: `POST` to the collection URL (`/films`) creates a new resource, and the server usually assigns the id. The data goes in the request body.

questions.question: A film already exists and you only want to change its `title`, leaving every other field alone. Which request fits best?
questions.explanation: `PATCH` applies a *partial* update to an existing resource. (`PUT` replaces the whole resource, so you would have to send every field.)

questions.question:
What does the following request do?

```http
DELETE /films/42
```
options: Returns the film with id 42 and marks it as deleted in your browser
Replaces film 42 with an empty film
questions.explanation: `DELETE` asks the server to remove the resource identified by the URL. There is usually no request body.

questions.question: Which of these methods typically send data to the server in a **request body**? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: `POST` (the new resource) and `PATCH` (the fields to change) carry a JSON body. `GET` and `DELETE` identify what they act on through the URL, so they normally have no body.

questions.question:
Why is this endpoint a bad design?

```http
GET /films/42/delete
```
options: URLs should never contain the word `films`
`GET` requests must always include a body
It is fine; `GET` is the most common method
`GET` is supposed to be safe. Browsers, caches, and link prefetchers may issue GET requests on their own, which could delete data by accident
questions.explanation: Use the method to express the action (`DELETE /films/42`) instead of putting a verb in the URL. Because `GET` is assumed to be harmless, tools freely repeat or pre-load it.

questions.question: Which URL design is the most RESTful way to get all films with a PG rating?
questions.explanation: URLs name *resources* (nouns), and query parameters filter or sort a collection. The method (`GET`) says what you're doing.

questions.question: A `POST` request successfully creates a new film. Which status code is the most appropriate response?
questions.explanation: `201 Created` specifically means a new resource was created. (`200` isn't wrong in practice, but `201` is the convention.)

questions.question: You send `GET /films/99999` and no film with that id exists. What should a well-designed API return?
questions.explanation: `404 Not Found` means the resource you asked for doesn't exist. `4xx` codes mean the *client* made the mistake; `5xx` codes mean the server failed.

questions.question: You call `DELETE /films/42` twice in a row. The first call succeeds. Which statement describes REST best practice?
options: `DELETE` is *idempotent*: after one or more calls, the end state is the same (film 42 is gone), even if the second call reports `404`
The second call will delete a different film
`DELETE` is not allowed to be called twice
The second call should create film 42 again
questions.explanation: Idempotent means repeating the request doesn't change the result beyond the first call. `POST`, by contrast, is *not* idempotent: calling it twice usually creates two records.

questions.question: In FastAPI, which decorator would you use for an endpoint that updates only some fields of an existing film?
questions.explanation: FastAPI decorators are named after the HTTP method: `get`, `post`, `patch`, `put`, and `delete`. There is no `update` decorator.

questions.question: You send JSON in a `POST` request body, but the server responds with `422 Unprocessable Entity`. What is the most likely cause?
options: The JSON is missing a required field or has a field of the wrong type, so the server's validation rejected it
questions.explanation: FastAPI returns `422` when the request body fails validation against the Pydantic model. The response body usually says which field was wrong, so read it.

questions.question: When you send a JSON body with `POST` or `PATCH`, which request header tells the server how to interpret it?
questions.explanation: `Content-Type` describes the format of the body you are *sending*. Without it, many servers won't parse the JSON.
